title: Preference Learning from Physics-Based Feedback: Tuning Language Models to Design BCC/B2 Superalloys
experiments_summary: The study follows a two-stage fine-tuning pipeline applied to three open instruction-tuned local language models (LLaMA-3.1-8B, Gemma-2-9B, OLMo-2-7B). Stage 1 (SFT): A cold-start dataset of approximately 55,000 (BCC composition / B2 composition / B2 volume %) triplets was constructed by filtering 207 BCC and 88 B2 compositions from the Materials Project to include only those with elements in the Thermo-Calc TCHEA7 database and energies above the convex hull between 0 and 0.25 eV/atom. Compositions were verified with Thermo-Calc to confirm >99% phase purity. All BCC–B2 pairs were combined with three sampled B2 volume fractions (uniformly drawn from 20–70%), yielding ~55,000 triplets. Models were fine-tuned using a causal language modeling objective with LoRA adapters (rank=8, alpha=32) targeting query and value projections, using 8-bit quantization across three NVIDIA A40 GPUs for ~93 hours over 5 epochs. Stage 2 (DPO): 5,000 (BCC/B2/B2 vol%) triples were sampled from each SFT model and evaluated using Thermo-Calc across temperatures 373K–2273K. A scalar reward was computed based on four hierarchically weighted synthesis feasibility criteria: BCC/B2 phase coexistence, BCC forming first, B2 existing at room temperature, and <10% non-BCC/B2 phases; the final refinement criterion was minimum lattice parameter mismatch. The top 25% of scored generations (1,250 samples) were paired with 100 randomly selected lower-ranked generations each, producing 125,000 preference pairs. DPO was performed for 1 epoch using the same LoRA and quantization configuration, with beta=0.5. Baselines included: (1) random search over BCC/B2 composition space; (2) few-shot prompting of GPT-4.1, GPT-O3, and Gemini-2.5; (3) prompt tuning of Gemini-2.5 using the MIPROv2 method from the DSPy library to encourage diversity; (4) a two-agent agentic system (generator + evaluator) using verbal reinforcement; and (5) outputs from prior published models Crystal-LLM and CDVAE, filtered to retain only compositions within the BCC/B2 TCHEA element space. Evaluation used compositional validity (Pauling electronegativity test), coverage recall and precision (Euclidean distance over Matminer-vectorized compositions against 18,216 possible alloys), novelty (pairwise distance from known alloys in the Materials Project), mean reward score, and unique BCC/B2 pair diversity at 100 generations. A diagnostic KL divergence analysis (forward D_KL between DPO and SFT policies on generated continuations, decomposed over domain-critical tokens such as element symbols and numerals) was also conducted to analyze OLMo's failure mode.
